title: Command Line Arguments
prompt:
Write a program to demonstrate the use of command line arguments
Sample Input: --name John --age 20
Sample Output: Name: John, Age: 20
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help you with that! Here's a Python program that demonstrates how to use command line arguments:

```python
import argparse

def main(name, age):
    """Print a greeting with the provided name and age."""
    print(f"Name: {name}, Age: {age}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Parse command line arguments
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Print a greeting with name and age.")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="The name of the person.")
    parser.add_argument("--age", type=int, required=True, help="The age of the person.")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Call the main function with the parsed arguments
    main(args.name, args.age)
```

When you run this program, you can provide command line arguments like this:

```
python main.py --name John --age 20
```

This will output:

```
Name: John, Age: 20
```

You can also provide arguments with spaces, special characters, or mixed case, and the program will still work correctly. The `--name` and `--age` arguments are required, so if you try to run the program without providing any arguments for those, it will raise an error.
